newsitem.title: UK: Goldman says it works with regulators on copper.
newsitem.headline: Goldman says it works with regulators on copper.

text.p: Goldman Sachs International said on Monday it is working with international regulators in the Sumitomo Corp copper affair and is not in any conflict with them.

"Since the beginning of or assignment for our client Sumitomo Corporation we have worked closely with regulators on both sides of the Atlantic. We are not in conflict with any authority," David Woods, Director European Media Relations, said in a news release.
Earlier on Monday Britain's Guardian newspaper said Sumitomo had assigned the US investment bank the task of unwinding huge holdings of copper.
Sumitomo said in June it had lost $1.8 billion - later raised to $2.6 billion - on what it alleges was unauthorised trading by Yasuo Hamanaka who built a long position in copper.
The Guardian's sources said Goldman had completely unwound the stockpile although the newspaper added that other traders disagreed.
The Guardian said there was no suggestion of impropriety on Goldman's part but that the assignment "seems to have led" it into conflict with agencies investigating the Hamanaka affair.
The Guardian said they might now regard Goldman as a source of information whilst it had had to instruct lawyers in relation to business carried out by its commodity dealing arm J. Aron and Co.
